text:
alex_chu: Ran an nsys capture against the prod batcher this morning. Seeing repeated H2D memcpy stalls on copy-stream 4 that line up with CPU wakeups ~1.1s apart. Snippet of timeline pasted below. Anyone seen prefetcher-induced serialization like this?

sam_w: can you paste the nsys range (nvtx) or the host-side trace slice? curious which thread is doing the prefetch + what core it's running on.

alex_chu: pasted quick excerpt from timeline:
```
[nsys] Time 1.102s: cudaMemcpyAsync H2D stream=4 size=1.2MB host-pinned=true start=1.102012 end=1.102450
[nsys] Time 1.102s: kernel conv_fwd stream=7 start=1.102470 end=1.103200
[nsys] CPU wakeup: thread prefetcher tid=9240 core=2 wake=1.102000 sleep_start=0.301000 sleep_duration=0.800s
[nsys] Time 2.203s: cudaMemcpyAsync H2D stream=4 start=2.203100 end=2.203540
```
This pattern repeats every ~1.101s, causing the copy engine to be idle between memcpy calls and kernels to be serialized behind copies.

miriam: that looks like the prefetch worker is sleeping between batches (sleep_for or condvar wait timeout) and not getting scheduled in time to feed the copy stream. Could be prefetch stride too big so the worker yields often.

ben_perf: did we recently change batching heuristic or the prefetch stride? I remember commit 0f3a changed prefetcher to use a timed yield to avoid CPU spin. That would explain regular gaps.

raj_k: yep, the rollout 0f3a (prefetch:use-timed-yield) landed in staging yesterday. Metrics show tail-latency spike: memcpy-stall-time p95 jumped from 1.2ms -> 4.1ms on some workloads.

sam_w: can you correlate kernel IDs with stream IDs? If kernels use high-priority stream and copies use low-priority, the copy engine idle might still block due to host-side scheduling gaps. Also check if host pinned pool is exhausted so allocations block.

alex_chu: good call, I checked pinned pool: ~85% utilization but not exhausted. Kernel stream=7 uses default priority, copy stream=4 uses copy engine with priority -1 (default). Noticed occasional host allocation latency spikes ~200us when pool hits fragmentation.

ben_perf: short actionable items: 1) Revert timed-yield in prefetcher and run perf baseline, 2) add NVTX ranges around prefetcher ops so we can slice traces by thread, 3) test with `ALLOCATOR_PINNED_PREALLOC=1` to rule out fragmented pinned alloc overhead.

miriam: alternative: switch prefetcher to use a hybrid wait: `condition_variable` + max spin (~50us) instead of sleeping for 800us. That keeps latency low without big CPU burn.

perf-bot: ALERT: memcpy-stall-rate increased by 2.9x vs baseline for job batcher-prod-13. See /alerts/1234 (auto-detected from nightly profile).

sam_w: for repro: run `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=batcher-prefetch --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none --duration=20s` while driving steady traffic. Then open timeline and filter for stream 4 and thread tid=9240.

alex_chu: I'll run the capture with NVTX marks and also try pinned prealloc env var. Planning to rollback 0f3a on a canary to confirm.

raj_k: if rollback confirms, we need a proper fix in the prefetcher (hybrid wait) + a unit test that catches heavy scheduling gaps in CI. Add perf test capturing p95 memcpy stall.

ben_perf: note: also consider moving prefetch to a dedicated core affinity (sched_setaffinity) for hot instances — cheap win for tail latency.

alex_chu: thanks all — will upload the full nsys .qdrep to the #eng-runtime artifacts channel once done and tag you. For now: action items: revert on canary, run capture with NVTX, try `ALLOCATOR_PINNED_PREALLOC=1`, and prototype hybrid wait.

miriam: ping when you have captures — happy to help analyze waterfall and CPU wakeups. :eyeglasses:

sam_w: add `--capture-range=sampling` if you want lower overhead traces but we need NVTX to find the prefetch boundaries.

alex_chu: noted — thanks.
